Without a doubt, it was a strong showing from the Sixers and now they move up to 40 at home. The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting Los Angeles Clippers, 122 - 113, at Wells Fargo Center on Thursday evening. The Sixers got out to a solid start at home, as they held the upper hand for the entire first quarter, before taking a 34 - 30 lead into the second. They took off in the second, as they quickly pushed their lead to 10, and went on to outscore the Clippers by 11 in the quarter, to take a 72 - 57 lead into halftime. However, the Clippers came out strong in the third, as they kicked off the quarter with an 11 - 4 run, to cut the gap to eight. They kept battling and managed to trim the deficit to just four points, as they trailed 90 - 86 heading into the final frame. Despite the Clippers' strong push, the Sixers kept it together and managed to push their lead back to 11, less two minutes into the quarter. From there, the Clippers were only able to get within three points, as the 76ers went on to their fifth home win of the season. Joel Embiid led Philadelphia with 41 points, 13 rebounds, four blocks and one assist, in 33 minutes. J.J. Redick followed up with 18 points, in 34 minutes off the bench, while Ben Simmons tallied 14 points, 11 assists, three rebounds and one steal. The Sixers shot 47 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 27 from long range. Meanwhile, Lou Williams led the Clippers with 26 points on 9 - of - 19 shooting, in 24 minutes off the bench. Danilo Gallinari followed up with 25 points, eight rebounds and one assist, in 35 minutes, while Tobias Harris added 24 points, eight rebounds, three assists and one block. The Clippers shot 44 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 23 from long range. The Clippers (4 - 4) will be right back in action, as they take on the Magic in Orlando on Friday. The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 133 - 132, in overtime at Wells Fargo Center on Friday evening. The 76ers (8 - 5) found themselves at the scene of the majority of their successes Friday, as they'd come into the contest with a perfect 60 record at home. After a nip - and - tuck first quarter, Philadelphia seemingly turned the game in their favor with a 32 - 17 advantage in the second period. To their credit, the Hornets (6 - 6) wouldn't go away, chipping away at their deficit until overcoming it in the fourth quarter. Cody Zeller matched Hernangomez's scoring and rebounding totals, while Michael Kidd-Gilchrist generated a 12 - point, 12 - rebound double - double off the bench. Embiid led the Sixers with a 42 - point, 18 - rebound double - double that also included four assists and four blocks. Ben Simmons tallied a 22 - point, 13 - assist double - double that also included eight boards, three blocks and two steals. Dario Saric contributed 18 points, nine rebounds, two assists and one block. J.J. Redick finished with 17 points, four assists and two rebounds. Markelle Fultz and Robert Covington started but only had seven points each.
